title: Preliminary Approval of Rules Governing Licensed Legal Paraprofessionals and Licensed Court-Access Assistants (Misc. Docket No. 24-9050)
author: Supreme Court of Texas

dom.t: Work redesign: Jagged capability demands selective deployment

st.t: Work redesign: Jagged capability demands selective deployment
st.an: The source does not assess legal AI’s jagged capabilities or selective deployment. Instead, it addresses the justice gap through a materially different human-service model: licensed non-attorneys providing bounded legal assistance under scope, sponsorship, disclosure and reporting safeguards.
qs: Many individuals have incomes low enough to qualify for assistance from legal aid and volunteer attorney organizations, but resources and staffing constraints allow these organizations to serve only a small fraction of qualified applicants.

st.t: Licensed alternatives: Expanded practice retains accountability
st.an: The Texas rules directly support the cluster’s proposition by creating licensed, subject-bounded nonlawyer practice for low-income clients while retaining competence requirements, limited-scope safeguards, escalation duties and disciplinary accountability. As preliminary regulatory provisions, they establish a design rather than evidence of improved access or outcomes.
qs: As set forth in this Section, a legal paraprofessional licensed by the Court may provide limited legal services to clients with low income.

kp.k: New licensed providers proposed to narrow the justice gap
kp.d: The Court proposes qualified non-lawyer provision of limited legal services to low-income individuals because legal aid and volunteer organizations cannot meet demand. It reports the Legal Services Corporation's figure that 92% of low-income Americans have unmet civil legal needs and concludes that licensing additional providers will help narrow the gap. This is a regulatory proposal and anticipated benefit, not evidence of achieved outcomes; the document does not discuss AI.
qs: The Legal Services Corporation reported recently that 92% of low-income Americans have unmet civil legal needs.

For years, the Court has made combating this “justice gap” a top priority, and it has become clear that we must think beyond traditional efforts—such as funding and volunteer work—and focus on reforms that will help bridge the justice gap with new providers.

kp.k: Rules remain preliminary and subject to public comment
kp.d: The August 6, 2024 order proposes new State Bar Articles XV and XVI and amendments to Texas Rules of Civil Procedure 500.4 and 510.4. It anticipates, rather than establishes, a December 1, 2024 effective date and permits changes following comments. The supplied document's introductory note identifies a separate November 4, 2024 delay order, whose substantive text is not included here.
qs: The Court will issue an order finalizing the new and amended rules after the close
The Court may change the new and amended rules in response to public comments. The Court expects the new and amended rules to take effect on December 1, 2024.

kp.k: Paraprofessional licensing combines alternative entry routes with subject specialization
kp.d: Applicants must have a high school diploma or equivalent, be at least 18, be authorized to work lawfully in the United States, and satisfy one of several educational, certification or experience routes, including a bachelor's degree or higher. Licenses are specific to family law, estate-planning and probate law, or consumer-debt law. Each subject requires relevant TBLS certification, Texas paralegal experience dedicating at least 50% of work in 3 of the past 5 years to that subject, or approved training.
qs: No general licensure as a legal paraprofessional is available.
have been employed as a paralegal in Texas and dedicated at least 50% of the applicant’s work in 3 of the past 5 years to the subject matter;
have completed training approved by the Court or the State Bar for the subject matter.

kp.k: Competence safeguards include examinations and character screening
kp.d: Paraprofessional applicants require present good moral character and fitness, an ethics examination and ordinarily a subject-matter examination. Screening considers criminal history, professional discipline, unauthorized-practice reports and other specified information. Subject-examination exemptions include a score of 260 on the Texas State Bar Examination, another examination testing the subject, or another State Bar exemption standard. Five failures ordinarily bar licensure in the relevant category, subject to waiver for good cause.
qs: To be eligible for licensure as a legal paraprofessional, an applicant must have present good moral character and fitness.
The ethics examination covers the Code of Ethics in Section 9 and other ethics rules, including ethics related to a licensed legal paraprofessional’s permitted activities under Section 7.
For good cause, the State Bar may waive this prohibition.

kp.k: Paraprofessional clients face income eligibility and disclosure requirements
kp.d: Proposed Article XV limits services to clients at or below 200% of federal poverty guidelines. Clients must self-certify eligibility by affidavit or an authorized unsworn declaration. Paraprofessionals must use written engagement agreements disclosing non-lawyer status and limited representation, and provide a State Bar-approved brochure explaining the program and complaint channels.
qs: “Low income” means at or below 200% of the federal poverty guidelines as published annually by the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services.
enter into a written engagement agreement with the client explaining that the licensed legal professional is not a lawyer and describing the limited scope of the representation;

kp.k: Justice-court representation can proceed without lawyer supervision
kp.d: A paraprofessional licensed in any available subject may represent eligible clients in civil justice-court suits without lawyer supervision. Permitted work includes preparation, litigation, settlement, communications with opposing parties or representatives, perfecting appeals to county court, and post-judgment collection, discovery and receiverships. The authorization to perfect an appeal is not stated as a general authorization to litigate the appeal in county court.
qs: A legal paraprofessional licensed by the Court in any of the available subject matters may represent a client, without lawyer supervision, in a civil suit in justice court, including:
perfecting an appeal of a judgment to the county court;
handling post-judgment collection, discovery, and receiverships.

kp.k: Family-law authority varies with complexity and supervision
kp.d: Family-law licensees may handle specified work in uncontested divorces without children or complex property issues without supervision, but preparing retirement-division QDROs requires lawyer review. Specified uncontested protective-order and parent–child proceedings require supervision; parent–child matters must involve standard conservatorship, possession and guideline support, and exclude cases involving the Texas Department of Family and Protective Services. Supervision requires review of every document before filing, identification of the lawyer in filings and availability for questions, but not court attendance.
qs: “Complex property issues” means that the suit involves a third-party sale or title transfer of real estate.
It does not mean that the supervising lawyer is required to appear, whether in person or electronically, for court proceedings.
If not preparing a QDRO, the licensed legal paraprofessional must advise the client to seek prompt assistance from a lawyer.

kp.k: Probate and consumer-debt work receive bounded independent authorization
kp.d: Estate-planning and probate licensees may independently advise on and file enumerated documents, including powers of attorney, transfer-on-death deeds, small estate affidavits and muniment-of-title applications, alongside other approved forms. Court representation is authorized for uncontested muniment-of-title proceedings. Consumer-debt licensees may independently assist with approved forms and represent clients in uncontested consumer-debt proceedings outside justice courts, with related communications permitted.
qs: represent a client in an uncontested court proceeding related to a muniment of title;
A legal paraprofessional licensed by the Court in consumer-debt law may provide, without lawyer supervision, the following limited legal services in courts other than justice courts:
represent a client in an uncontested court proceeding related to consumer debt;

kp.k: Scope limits trigger client protection and escalation
kp.d: Paraprofessionals appearing before or communicating with courts must file and serve a signed notice identifying the license, client and limited tasks. When work exceeds authorized scope, they must notify clients of scope problems and deadlines, supply service information, seek extensions where appropriate, direct clients to resources and surrender client papers and property. Work wholly outside authorized scope requires moving to withdraw or adding a lawyer in charge.
qs: The notice must be served on all parties.
requesting an extension or continuance from the court, as appropriate;

kp.k: Paraprofessionals face ethics, discipline and continuing education duties
kp.d: The proposal imposes competence, independent-judgment, candor, confidentiality, conflicts and truthful-communications obligations, prohibits immigration services, and bars compensation for preparing instruments affecting real-property title under Texas Government Code § 83.001. Courts may sanction paraprofessionals like lawyers; the State Bar investigates complaints and may suspend or revoke licenses. Annual renewal requires dues, at least 3 ethics education hours, at least 7 hours in each licensed subject, and client-service reporting. Lawyer–client privilege rules extend to authorized work.
qs: A licensed legal paraprofessional must not provide immigration services.
A licensed legal paraprofessional may be sanctioned by a court in the same manner as a lawyer.
complete at least 3 hours of continuing education on ethics;
complete at least 7 hours of continuing education in each subject matter in which the licensed legal paraprofessional is licensed to practice;

kp.k: Court-access assistants follow an organization-sponsored supervised model
kp.d: Article XVI creates a distinct route requiring approved justice-court training, a criminal-history background check and sponsorship by an approved legal assistance organization. Eligible sponsors include qualifying nonprofits, Texas law-school clinics or pro bono programs, and bar pro bono projects. Assistants may perform trained legal services in civil justice-court suits under a sponsoring organization's lawyer, with written non-lawyer disclosure and client consent. Supervising lawyers must be available for questions but need not attend court; sponsors must adopt supervision policies.
qs: provide a certificate of sponsorship by an approved legal assistance organization.
informs all clients in writing that the court-access assistant is not a lawyer;
obtains written consent from the client to their representation by a non-lawyer.
A sponsoring approved legal assistance organization must adopt policies for lawyer supervision of its licensed court- access assistants.

kp.k: Sponsors fund and oversee court-access assistants
kp.d: Court-access assistants cannot directly charge clients or receive percentage, contingency or origination fees, but sponsoring organizations may pay them. Sponsors must require at least 3 hours of continuing education, report serious fitness concerns and sponsorship termination immediately, and report client numbers annually. Termination of sponsorship revokes the license, with reinstatement possible through another sponsor and a new application. Privilege protections apply to communications in authorized work.
qs: A licensed court-access assistant must not directly charge a client for services or claim or receive a percentage fee, contingency fee, or origination fee.
However, nothing in these rules is intended to prevent the licensed court-access assistant from being paid for services by the sponsoring approved legal assistance organization.
annually report the number of clients served by the licensed court-access assistants under this Article and any other data requested by the State Bar.

kp.k: Legal information remains distinct from licensed representation
kp.d: Both proposed licensing articles preserve people's ability to provide legal information, resources, referrals, educational materials, verbatim form recording, completeness checks and courthouse-navigation help. Article XV also states that it does not regulate lawyers' use of paralegals. Proposed civil-procedure amendments recognize the new licensed representatives and shift assisted self-representation toward permission unless the court finds good cause to deny it, while requiring the self-represented individual to attend.
qs: recording on forms verbatim;
reviewing forms and other documents for completeness and, if incomplete, stating why the form or document is incomplete;
regulating the use of paralegals by lawyers;
The self-represented individual must be present for any court proceeding in which assistance is provided.
